Hello /v/Gardening,

I'm curious about how you keep things like mosquitoes, black flies and other blood-seeking nasties off your person. I had hoped to see a reduction in the number of mosquitoes this year due to our late start to a truly warm season, but the mosquito population in particular has rallied to ensure that is not the case. So, from clothing choices, to traps, planting choices and beyond, I'd like to hear what you have to say. I am particularly interested in options that don't involve indiscriminate spraying of insecticide.

Additionally, strategies to repel garden insects are most welcome. Personally, I use as much companion planting as I can.
Bat houses and bird feeders! Bring in the bug's natural predators.

White nose syndrome has killed something like 99% of the bats in my province - which is really depressing. I suppose I've been lazy about putting up some of the seed feeders that I've got kicking around. I'd like to hang them in my willow tree; but I'm not certain if there are rules to follow where hanging bird feeders are concerned.

We have bats and tons of birds, but the problem is that they don't actually eat mosquitoes if there are bigger and juicer bugs to go after. Since we also have a lot of flies and moths and beetles of various sorts, they would attract the predators more. The mosquitoes are so small, they aren't much of a meal.

This will sound crazy but we use [kerosene lantern's(]http://www.amazon.com/Rothco-Kerosene-Lantern-in-Red/dp/B008RBEUTQ), Learned from my dad. And if you can't get the lantern use a mason jar with a bit of rag filled with kerosene. I think the kerosene has a smell bugs hate.
I think that I have kerosene mixed with orange oil for some tiki torches. I should check that.

I have tried a few of the mosquito repellent plants...good article here. I don't know if they actually work...hard to say when there might have been bigger swarms if we didn't have the plants.

I try to avoid being outside right at dusk since they are the worst then, especially those smaller, faster little nasty ones that leave itchier, smaller hives. Little bastards. When I'm working in wetter areas of the garden I resort to deep woods off. They have a dry formula that is much less gooey when applied. I don't like using all that DEET, but it's better than getting west Nile virus, I figure.

I read the same article! I actually have lemon balm, catnip, mint and bee balm in hanging baskets on the four corners of my raised beds. I've also got marigolds acting as sentry around the perimeter. I'm doing everything I can to avoid using DEET. In fact, I'm considering trying to refine catnip oil; as it has been demonstrated to be more effective than DEET. I'm a ways off of production, though.

Left handed

Loft: 9.5 (D4 setting)

Shaft: Diamana white 70 s flex

Looks: Coming off the white Taylormade R11, it was nice to get back to a traditional black crown. The club is beautiful to look at and the markings are very minor and not distracting at all. The active recoil channel (ARC) is pretty cool and I though was a gimmick but, as I'll explain later, I was wrong. Side note, the headcover looks great as well.

Feel: I like the heavier shaft. It makes me focus on tempo a lot more. Easy to handle and you feel in control of the club's face. You can feel a miss-hit but the ARC dampens the sting for sure and for me reduces a devastating ball flight to a manageable miss. A slice is still a slice, but I feel confident not hitting it square every single time. There is not a lot of pop off the face but the ball still seems to hiss at initial takeoff which might confuse some.

Sound: Biggest con. This thing is loud. It pings and everyone knows when you are hitting. Not the best quality and rumor has it the 913 has a much better sound.

Adjustability: Titleist still uses a confusing letter number combination system but with the included book you can easily figure out what each setting is doing.

Price: Expensive at $450, but I see it as a very long term investment. The club feels solid and I can't see me having to replace it any time soon.

What did I miss? Let me know and I will answer the questions as best I can.
